newsitem.title: POLAND: BEIERSDORF TO BUY 29.4 PCT OF POLISH FIRM.
newsitem.headline: BEIERSDORF TO BUY 29.4 PCT OF POLISH FIRM.

text.p: Germany's Beiersdorf AG signed on August 6 a letter of intent with the Polish National Investment Fund Octava to buy a 29.4 percent stake in the Pollena Lechia cosmetics-maker for 50 million marks, the Octava fund said.

"Beiersdorf AG of Germany and Poland's NFI Octava signed yesterday a letter of intent concerning Beiersdorf's strategic entry into Pollena Lechia SA," the fund, which holds 33 percent of Pollena Lechia, said in a Thursday statement.

"Under the terms of the letter of intent, Beiersdorf will initially invest 50 million marks in Pollena Lechia. The investor will hold an initial 29.4 percent interest in the company, combined with voting and management control," it said.

The fund, one of 15 created under Poland's mass privatisation programme, said that under the agreement Pollena Lechia would be floated on the Warsaw bourse within 19 months of Beiersdorf's entry into the firm.
The fund said Beiersdorf would buy Pollena Lechia's new share issue, expected in October, after the final agreement between Octava and the German firm was reached in September.
Pollena Lechia's principal products are a range of skin creams sold under the Nivea trade mark, Colodent toothpaste and Bambino baby care products.
Pollena Lechia's had sales last year of 185 million zlotys and on a net profit of 17 million zlotys.

"Beiersdorf is the ideal strategic partner for Pollena Lechia as it can integrate the company into its multinational marketing capabilities and know-how, particularly with respect to the Nivea trademark," the statement quoted Uwe Wolfer, member of the Beiersdorf management board, as saying.
"Our objective will be to transform Pollena Lechia into the leading company in the Polish personal care market," he said.
After Pollena's capital rise Beiersdorf's would have 29.4 percent of the firm, the Octava fund 25 percent, the 14 other funds 21 percent and the state treasury 19 percent.
The rest would be in the hands of the employees.
